description: Flappy Bird online free: tap to flap a little yellow bird through the green pipes. One pipe cleared is one point. How far can you fly?
lede: The one-tap classic, in your browser. A little yellow bird, a row of green pipes, and one button: tap to flap. Each pipe you thread is a point, each tap too many is a crash, and the pipes keep coming faster the further you fly. It takes ten seconds to learn and a lot longer to master, and your best flight is saved, so there is always one more pipe to beat.

p: Press Start flapping and the bird is in the air. Tap anywhere, click, or press Space to flap its wings and lift it a little; between flaps gravity pulls it back down. Steer the bird through the gap in each green pipe. Every pipe you clear is one point, shown in big numbers at the top of the screen.
Touch a pipe or the ground and the flight is over. You see how many pipes you cleared, which medal that earns, and whether you beat your best flight, which is saved on this device.

The pipes start drifting towards the bird at about 132 pixels a second, with a gap of 205 pixels to fly through, and a new pipe arrives every 265 pixels. Each pipe you clear makes the next ones a little faster, up to about 200 pixels a second, so a flight that felt gentle at pipe five feels like a blur by pipe thirty.

The gap between the pipes never shrinks: the challenge is speed, not a tighter squeeze. The bird falls at up to 700 pixels a second, so late in a flight a single missed tap drops it further than you expect.

sections.h: The bird that broke the internet
p: Flappy Bird was made by Dong Nguyen, a Vietnamese developer working under the name .GEARS. He released it in May 2013, and for months almost nobody noticed. Then, in early 2014, it shot to the top of the free charts: it was reported to have been downloaded more than 50 million times, and at its peak it was said to earn about $50,000 a day from adverts.

In February 2014, at the height of its fame, Nguyen took the game down, saying its success had become too much. The removal only made it more famous: phones with the game still installed were listed for sale online, and a wave of clones filled the stores. The version here is the same idea, free in your browser: one tap, one bird, and pipes that do not forgive.

ol: Flap in a steady rhythm instead of tapping wildly. Short, even taps hold the bird near the middle of the gap.
Aim for the middle of each gap, not the top of it. The bird drops fast between taps, so flying high leaves no room to fall.
Look at the next pipe, not the bird. Your finger already knows the rhythm; your eyes should be a pipe ahead.
Do not flap twice in a row unless the bird is falling. A double flap sends it into the top pipe more often than it saves it.
On a phone, hold the device with both hands and tap with a thumb. One hand alone wobbles the screen at the worst moment.

p: For another test of quick reactions, see how fast you can tap when the signal comes in the [[reaction-time-test]]. If you would rather steer than flap, eat eggs and grow longer in the classic [[snake]]. You can find every fast, fairground-style game in [[cat:arcade|arcade games]].

faq: How do I make the bird fly?
Tap anywhere on the game, click, or press Space, Arrow Up or W. Each tap flaps the wings once and lifts the bird a little; between taps gravity pulls it down.
How fast do the pipes get?
They start at about 132 pixels a second and speed up by 2 pixels a second for each pipe you clear, up to about 200 pixels a second. The gap stays the same size.
10 pipes earns Bronze, 20 earns Silver, 30 earns Gold, and 40 or more earns Platinum. Under 10 pipes earns the Egg medal.
